# Results — Study 220 (Small Dogs of the Dow) on the real point-in-time tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Three strategies — the full
Dogs (top-10 yield), the Small Dogs (5 lowest-priced of the 10 Dogs), and the Foolish Four
(Dogs #2-#5 by price) — raced against the DIA total-return benchmark. **Total-return** prices,
trailing-12-month yield at the prior December close, **20 bps** on turnover, same-basis
benchmark (DIA total return). As-of **2026-06-13**; match the fingerprint to confirm you
hold the same tape.*

## Sample span & survivorship handling

- **Universe:** point-in-time Dow-30 membership timeline from Study 88 (anchored 1999-11-01,
  ~12 reshuffles replayed forward through 2025). Each January's Dogs are picked only from the
  members as of that January — no survivorship bias.
- **Sample:** **26 January rebalances, 2000 → 2025.**
- **Two members unrecoverable (named, not silent):** Eastman Kodak (2000–2004 member;
  bankrupt entity, no Yahoo tape) and Walgreens (2019–2024 member; taken private 2024). Both
  were plausible high-yielders; their absence is a real, named selection limitation.

| Series | Window | Shape | Fingerprint |

| Dow panel (total return + dividends) + DIA benchmark | 1999-12-01 → 2026-06-12 | 46 tickers × 6,673 days | `6dfd9e54cba6` |

## Headline results — 26 years, net of 20 bps/turnover

| Strategy | CAGR | Grew $1 → | vs Dow | Mean excess | Win rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Small Dogs (5 cheapest Dogs)** | **10.57%** | **$13.64** | **+3.04 pts/yr** | **+2.88%/yr** | **65% (17/26)** |
| Dogs of the Dow (top-10 yield) | 8.51% | $8.36 | +0.98 pts/yr | +0.87%/yr | 54% (14/26) |
| Foolish Four (Dogs #2-#5 by price) | 7.67% | $6.84 | +0.14 pts/yr | −0.11%/yr | 54% (14/26) |
| **Dow (DIA total return)** | **7.54%** | **$7.61** | — | — | — |

## Inference — Small Dogs vs Dow

| Test | Value | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| HAC *t* on annual excess (Small Dogs − Dow) | **+1.82** | Below the |t| ≥ 2 bar — not certifiable |
| Block-bootstrap 95% CI on mean excess | **[−0.27%, +5.63%]** (two-sided *p* = 0.07) | CI barely clips zero; suggestive but not significant |
| Alpha (Small Dogs ~ Dow) | **+5.26%/yr**, *t* = **+2.68** | Clears the bar, but alpha inflated by low beta (0.72) |
| Beta (Small Dogs ~ Dow) | **0.72** (R² = 0.59) | Defensive low-price tilt — less Dow risk |

## Incremental test — Small Dogs vs full Dogs

| Test | Value | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Mean Small Dogs − Dogs | **+2.01%/yr** | The price filter adds ~2 pts over the yield filter alone |
| HAC *t* (Small Dogs − Dogs annual excess) | **+2.40** | Clears the bar — but this is a derived series with data-mining baggage |
| Block-bootstrap 95% CI | **[+0.41%, +3.71%]** (two-sided *p* = 0.01) | Consistent with a real low-price tilt |

## Inference — Foolish Four vs Dow

| Test | Value | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| HAC *t* (Foolish Four − Dow) | **−0.09** | Pure noise; this variant is dead |
| Mean annual excess | **−0.11%/yr** | Essentially flat vs the Dow |
| Foolish Four − Dogs | **−0.99%/yr**, *t* = **−0.80** | Underperforms the Dogs it was derived from |

## How to read it

- **Small Dogs shows a suggestive but sub-threshold signal vs the Dow.** The HAC t on the raw
  annual excess is +1.82 — close to, but below, the |t| ≥ 2 bar. The bootstrap 95% CI
  ([−0.27%, +5.63%]) barely touches zero from below with p = 0.07. The alpha-regression t of
  +2.68 clears the bar but is driven substantially by the low beta (0.72) — the Small Dogs
  are a lower-risk basket that earns more risk-adjusted return, not necessarily certified
  alpha above what the lower beta explains.
- **The incremental test (Small vs full Dogs) clears the bar at t = +2.40.** However, this
  is a derived test on a strategy originally published after fitting to the same historical
  data — a classic in-sample "discovery" that should attract heavy data-mining skepticism.
  Domian & Louton (1998) and McQueen, Shields & Thorley (1997) both found the extra edge
  from price-filtering vanished in out-of-sample or risk-adjusted tests.
- **The Foolish Four is demonstrated noise.** HAC t = −0.09 on its excess vs the Dow;
  the skip-the-cheapest quirk adds nothing — it subtracts. This is the canonical cautionary
  tale: a parameter optimised in-sample (skip #1, keep #2-#5) loses all power out-of-sample.
- **Verdict: Signal → Weak, Tradability → Mirage.**  The Small Dogs' edge looks interesting
  on the surface (+3 pts/yr, 26 years) but: (1) the HAC t on the annual excess sits at 1.82
  — below the house bar; (2) with three simultaneous strategy variants (Dogs/Small/Foolish)
  the effective multiple-comparison correction pushes all of them below threshold; (3) the
  small-cap / low-price tilt is replicable far more cheaply with any small-cap ETF; (4) a
  five-name equal-weight basket of the cheapest Dow names carries enormous idiosyncratic
  concentration risk and dividend-trap exposure; (5) the Foolish Four — the variant that
  attracted the most retail money in the 1990s — is completely flat. The honest read is
  Weak/Mirage.

## Reproduce

```bash
python examples/verify.py              # real tape (this doc)
pytest studies/220-small-dogs/tests -q # offline tests
```
